question: pr2879
answer:
The diff adds `proxy=` to `Client`, `AsyncClient`, and the top-level request, streaming, and HTTP verb helpers re-exported by `httpx`. A single proxy becomes an `all://` route. Both default transports now accept a string, `URL`, or `Proxy`, and `mounts=` is the documented migration path for custom routing. Legacy `proxies=` still works with a deprecation warning for truthy values. [httpx/_client.py](httpx/_client.py:674) · [httpx/_api.py](httpx/_api.py) · [httpx/__init__.py](httpx/__init__.py) · [httpx/_transports/default.py](httpx/_transports/default.py)

**Findings**

- **`proxies={}` can unexpectedly enable environment proxies.** Both constructors now pass `proxies or proxy` to `_get_proxy_map`. With no `proxy=`, an explicit empty mapping becomes `None`, so eligible clients can pick up `HTTP_PROXY`, `HTTPS_PROXY`, or `ALL_PROXY` and send traffic through an unintended proxy. The existing empty-map test runs with proxy environment variables cleared. [httpx/_client.py](httpx/_client.py:212) · [tests/client/test_proxies.py](tests/client/test_proxies.py:86) · [tests/conftest.py](tests/conftest.py:34)
- **The CLI rename breaks existing scripts.** The `httpx` entry point now accepts `--proxy` only. Python callers have a deprecation period, while scripts using `--proxies` fail argument parsing. [pyproject.toml](pyproject.toml:57) · [httpx/_main.py](httpx/_main.py:388)
- **The migration guide contains a syntax error** in its proxy-exclusion example and incorrectly says top-level helpers accept `mounts=`. Explicitly mounted transports also use their own TLS and connection settings, so migrating a proxy map can change behavior if callers relied on client-level settings. [docs/compatibility.md](docs/compatibility.md:168) · [httpx/_client.py](httpx/_client.py:695)

Both sync and async send paths use the resulting mount table, so routing changes also affect followed redirects. [httpx/_client.py](httpx/_client.py:1006) · [httpx/_client.py](httpx/_client.py:1738)

Static review only.
